name: One Piece
desc: The finale. Your place in the picture

text.y: You have come a long way. You don't need to put together the whole world. You need to find your piece.
text.t: You have come a long way. Here is what I understood while I was keeping this book: you don't need to put together the whole world. You need to find your piece.

body.y:
A doctor was about to retire. One night he stayed late at the hospital. And just then a mother and her baby needed his help. He stayed and helped.

The Baal Shem Tov said: sometimes a soul comes into the world for the sake of one good deed at the right moment.
body.t:
In the Israeli city of Rishon LeZion there was a doctor. He had half a year left before retirement. One day he stayed at the hospital until late at night. And exactly then a mother who was giving birth needed the help of an experienced doctor. He stayed and helped them both.

The Baal Shem Tov, the great teacher, said: sometimes a soul comes into the world for many years for the sake of one good deed, done at the right moment and in the right place.

steps.tr: “Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion.”

plain.y: Here is our word “chelek” again. To rejoice in your portion means to rejoice in your role in the puzzle and to develop it.
plain.t: Here is our word “chelek” again. Rejoicing in your portion does not mean sitting and doing nothing. It means rejoicing in your role in the puzzle and developing it to the full, without envying other people's roles.

steps.q: What does “rejoicing in your portion” mean to you?
options: Not envying what belongs to others
steps.r: Here is King Shlomo's answer. Not “all is vapour,” but “find your portion and rejoice in it.”

steps.title: The Rebbe and the ambassador
steps.body:
In 1972 the Lubavitcher Rebbe spoke with Israel's ambassador Yitzchak Rabin and brought up the mishnah “Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion.”

The essence of the explanation: rejoicing in your portion does not mean being content with little and stopping. It means rejoicing in your special role in the puzzle, unfolding your strengths to the full and not envying other people's roles.

steps.kicker: Kohelet 12:13 · The last words of the book
steps.title: One foundation, a portion for each

body.y:
סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע אֶת הָאֱלֹקִים יְרָא וְאֶת מִצְוֹתָיו שְׁמוֹר כִּי זֶה כָּל הָאָדָם

“Fear the Almighty and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.”

The foundation is the same for everyone. But each person has their own piece.
body.t:
סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע אֶת הָאֱלֹקִים יְרָא וְאֶת מִצְוֹתָיו שְׁמוֹר כִּי זֶה כָּל הָאָדָם

“The sum of the matter, when all has been heard: fear the Almighty and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.”

This is how the book ends. The common foundation is the same for everyone: the Torah and the mitzvot. But each person has their own portion. Just like on Sukkot: the etrog and the aravah fulfil one mitzvah, but each in its own way.

steps.he: כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.tr: “All Israel have a portion in the World to Come.”

plain.y: Here is our word חֵלֶק again. Everyone has a portion. Nobody is superfluous.
plain.t: The same word again: חֵלֶק. These words open the reading of every chapter of Pirkei Avot. The chain comes full circle: everyone has a portion in this world, their own piece of the puzzle, and everyone has a portion in the World to Come.

steps.q: What do you feel when you read this?
options: There is a place for me too
I want to take care of my portion
steps.r: That's how it is: in the Almighty's plan there are no superfluous pieces.
